pr_title: Use dictionary to track PackageRelationships instead of searching a list
pr_body:
This change adds an OrderedDictionary<TKey,TValue> type to System.IO.Packaging to keep a list of relationships that have been added, while ensuring that the ids are unique with decent performance characteristics. The current implementation searches a list which gets really slow with large numbers of relationships. A Dictionary by itself does not work for this as the order of addition is important. Thus, this combines a LinkedList to track the order, while a Dictionary is used to for quick look up of existing items.

Fixes #983

issue_context.title: System.IO.Packaging.InternalRelationshipCollection.GetRelationshipIndex doesn't scale
issue_context.body:
**Use case**
The Microsoft OpenXml SDK relies on the System.IO.Packaging API to generate Microsoft Excel files. This allows adding hyperlinks to Excel columns, but with the current resource consumption this is impossible when you have an excel sheet with about 100.000 records that each has a link to some additional record information - for instance a deep link to a HTTP resource. This API uses PackagePart.CreateRelationship inside the System.IO.Packaging stack.

**Background**
When adding hyperlinks to Excel cells, you have to call AddHyperlinkRelationship on the OpenXmlContainer. This will then follow the stack in System.IO.Packaging:
PackagePart.CreateRelationship -> InternalRelationshipCollection.Add -> InternalRelationshipCollection.ValidateUniqueRelationshipId -> InternalRelationshipCollection.GetRelationshipIndex.

**Problem**
ValidateUniqueRelationshipId  will call GetRelationshipIndex to ensure that the relationship id is unique, and it loops through all the links each time it is invoked. As the identifier list grows it will (obviously) become exponentially slower. Backing this identifier store by something similar to a HashSet would greatly improve the lookup time.

review_comments: Are there appropriate tests in place for all of this?
Yes, it's internal so no tests target it. But all code paths are executed via already existing tests.
Previously foreach'ing over an InternalRelationshipCollection would be non-allocating; now it'll result in an enumerator being allocated.  Are there any places where that was being done?
The only place this was used was promptly cast to an `IEnumerator` to be filtered elsewhere.

We have a `SortedDictionary` class, which is generic and implements `IEnumerable<T>`: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.sorteddictionary-2
Can you use that instead, or was there a reason why you decided against it?

Note: There is an `OrderedDictionary` class, but it's not generic, and I assume that's why you decided not to use it: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.specialized.ordereddictionary

Yes there was a reason :) Sorted dictionary does not ensure the order is the same as was added - its order is defined by some sort of comparer. The ordering is part of the current behavior and affects the order the relationships are persisted to the file/stream.

I've added a comment to the class summary to explain the difference.

As to using `System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary`, there are two issues:

1. It's non-generic. Annoying, but potentially ok. 
2. In order to remove an item, it is searching through the whole array. The implementation I've added just removes a node in the linked list, so it's `O(1)`
